title: Every exchange needs a defined end
statement: Give every open-ended task or exchange a defined end, such as a completed paragraph or a sign the idea is understood, so it doesn't run until someone gives up.
detail: In the reviewed Grade 9 prototype, a learner's substantively wrong second answer in a quote break-down conversation was half-corrected and the conversation moved on; nothing told the child or the app when the quote had been understood (`g9/library/text/L36b8ba.txt`, line 338). The review contrasts a stem-based task, which ends when the paragraph is complete, with a chat, which ends when someone gives up, and its build checklist asks for a convergence criterion so the break-down has a defined end point (lines 338 and 129). It does not say what that criterion should be.

evidence.quote: and the Archivist half-corrects, then moves on. Nothing tells the child, or the app, when the quote has been understood. A stem-based task ends when the paragraph is complete; a chat ends when someone gives up.
